Subject: POC eval methodology alignment / next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed evaluation plan so we can lock owners and dates. High-level: Acme wants a 2-week POC to validate accuracy, latency, and safe output behavior for the assistant use case we demoed (customer support triage + product recommendations).

Proposed evaluation plan (attached: acme-poc-eval-plan.xlsx):
- Goal: confirm model meets production thresholds and integration readiness for December launch.
- Success criteria (proposed):
  - Accuracy / intent match >= 90% on prioritized intents
  - Latency p95 < 300ms for end-to-end API responses
  - Hallucination / incorrect confident answers <= 3% on sampled queries
  - Human escalation rate <= 5% for customer-facing flows
- Eval methodology options:
  1) Offline evaluation: curated & labeled test set; quantitative metrics (precision/recall, F1) + manual adjudication for corner cases.
  2) Online shadowing: mirror a percentage of live traffic to Redwood in shadow mode to measure real-world latency, behavior, and fallback rates (no user-visible changes).
  We recommend doing both: a focused offline eval to validate core correctness, followed by a short online shadow to validate latency and operational characteristics.

Proposed timeline:
- Mon Mar 8: 30-min kickoff (agree to owners, data access, and final rubric)
- Tue–Fri Mar 9–13: Offline eval on a seeded/sanitized test set (labeling + rubric scoring)
- Mon–Fri Mar 15–19: Online shadow (live mirror at low %), collect metrics and human review samples
- Mon Mar 22: Review results and decide next steps (rollout vs. extend POC)

Owners (proposed):
- Acme: Priya Singh (Product lead), Alex Johnson (Data/ops)
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (POC lead / product), Rachel Kim (Solutions / evals), Neha Kapoor (SRE / infra)

Open questions we need from your side:
1) Which eval methodology do you prefer as the primary signal (offline first vs. shadow-first)?
2) Can you provide a sanitized sample dataset and expected success intents by Mon Mar 9?
3) Any specific security/compliance requirements for shadowing (VPC peering, IP allowlist, SOC 2 constraints)?

If that looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff and share the rubric (attached: redwood-eval-rubric.pdf) and the evaluation spreadsheet.

Thanks —

Marissa — thanks for the clear plan and the attachments. Quick answers and a few clarifications from our side: we like the dual approach you outlined (offline + shadow) but want online shadow to be the primary signal for ops/latency. Offline eval is useful for edge-case labeling.

Proposed success metrics from Acme:
- Intent / intent-match >= 92% on our prioritized query set
- Latency p95 end-to-end < 250ms for the majority of production flows
- Hallucination/confident incorrect responses < 2% on customer-facing flows
- Human escalation rate < 2% for high-value customers

Questions / constraints:
1) We can provide a sanitized 10k sample dataset by Mon Mar 9, but will need an NDA addendum for certain PII fields (Priya will coordinate).
2) For shadowing, we prefer either VPC peering (if Redwood supports) or a secure mutual-TLS endpoint. Can you confirm options and an emergency fallback?
3) We’d like to run shadow at 5–10% traffic initially. Is there any special config required on our side?

We can do kickoff Mon Mar 8; Priya and Mike will join. If possible, please share a calendar invite for 10am PT.

Thanks —

Thanks Marissa & Alex — quick note from Redwood solutions on the grading rubric and operational items. Attaching the detailed rubric (redwood-eval-rubric.pdf) but key points here so we can align in kickoff: 

Proposed rubric (weights):
- Correctness / intent-match: 50% (measured via labeled test set; F1/accuracy on intents)
- Latency & reliability: 20% (p95 latency, error rate)
- Hallucination / safety: 20% (manual adjudication on sampled outputs; critical failures counted higher)
- Human escalation rate / usability: 10% (percent routed to human agent or manual correction)

Offline vs online (operational differences):
- Offline: static labeled set, expedited scoring, good for measuring correctness and edge-case behavior. Lower operational risk.
- Online shadow: mirrors production traffic so we can measure latency, cold-starts, and fallback interactions. Needs data access path (VPC peering or mutual-TLS) and a plan for tokenization / logging retention.

On the technical side we’ll own the Redwood deployment and can run in A) hosted shadow mode via secure API + IP allowlist or B) private peering if you prefer we host inside your VPC (requires infra setup). Neha will scope the infra work and will follow up with a short checklist.

Suggested slight timeline update to make room for dataset delivery / compliance review:
- Kickoff: Mon Mar 8 10:00am PT (30m)
- Offline baseline: Mar 9–13 (labeling + scoring)
- Shadow window: Mar 16–20 (give one extra day to ensure infra readiness)
- Results review: Mar 23

If that works, I’ll update the spreadsheet with the metric targets Alex listed and add a column for pass/fail thresholds.

—Rachel Kim
